summary: UI for TTS Speech Specification
description:
h2. Intro There could be many reasons why to specify a certain text for TTS: # Equations # symbols / units # Languages with different number names per gender (e.g. Icelandic, Hebrew) # Singular / plural # etc Consider the following item: !Screenshot 2026-01-08 at 12.32.38.png|width=328,alt="Screenshot 2026-01-08 at 12.32.38.png"! In the first line we want the distance to be read “one meter”, while in the second line we want “three meter{color:#ff5630}s{color}”. Currently, to to that, we need to wrap the element in discussion in the following way: {code:html} ...element... {code} So for our item, we should do: {code:html}The distance between points A and B is 1m
The distance between points B and C is 3m
{code} Besides needing to enable the source editor, this requires messing up with the HTML code, which might end up bad very quickly. ---- The idea behind this ticket is to create a UI for this process, so we can avoid HTML editing when it’s possible. As a content creator, I would like to: # Enter my text # Highlight the relevant element (e.g. “3m”) # Click on a toolbar button: !Screenshot 2026-01-08 at 12.44.45.png|width=1002,alt="Screenshot 2026-01-08 at 12.44.45.png"! # Get a popup box in which I can enter the relevant text (e.g. “three meters”) # Confirm / OK / Done # Have the highlighted part wrapped with the span element, done behind the scenes

summary: [TAO Authoring] Improved test assembly items search

Enhance asset selection search across resources
description:
{panel:bgColor=#deebff}
Improvement of search capabilities across assets when inserting into another resource, including search by metadata, partial name/label, etc.

*Why it matters*: reduces time spent hunting items; increases reuse.

*Goal:* TAO should improve asset search capabilities when authors insert an asset into another resource (item, shared stimulus, etc.), making it easier to find the right asset using richer, more flexible search criteria.

This feature extends the current search capabilities so that authors can more efficiently locate assets when inserting them into items or other resources. The improvement should support search by metadata, partial name or label, and other relevant attributes, reducing the time spent manually browsing large asset libraries. In addition, when a user changes an asset that is already assigned, the search should open in the folder containing the asset, with the current asset selected.
{panel}

{panel:bgColor=#eae6ff}
*As a* TAO author

*I want* to be able to search assets (images, audios, videos, shared stimuli) more effectively when inserting them into another resource

*so* that I can quickly find the correct asset, improve reuse, and reduce time spent hunting through the asset repository.
{panel}

{panel:bgColor=#e3fcef}
*Acceptance criteria* {color:#FF991F}*[ UX NEEDED ]*{color}

# {color:#FF5630}*[ MUST ]*{color} *GIVEN* an author is inserting an asset into another resource in TAO 3.x
*WHEN* the user opens the asset selection dialog
*THEN* the system provides search capabilities that help locate assets efficiently
*AND* browse capability to select a folder and see its contents
# {color:#FF5630}*[ MUST ]*{color} *GIVEN* the asset selection dialog displays a list of assets, with or without a search applied
*WHEN* assets are displayed from the selected folder or as search results, including assets located in subfolders
*THEN* the dialog shall display at least the following fields for each asset:
#* Label
#* Location
#* Last modified on
# {color:#FF5630}*[ MUST ]*{color} *GIVEN* an author is inserting an asset into another resource in TAO 3.x
*WHEN* the user opens the asset selection dialog
*THEN* the search and its filters apply to the folder selected in the dialog and all subfolders
# {color:#FF5630}*[ MUST ]*{color} *GIVEN* an author is inserting an asset into another resource in TAO 3.x
*WHEN* the user searches by a partial asset name or label
*THEN* the system returns matching assets based on partial text, not only exact matches
# {color:#FF5630}*[ MUST ]*{color} *GIVEN* an author is inserting an asset into another resource in TAO 3.x
*WHEN* the user searches using available metadata fields
*THEN* the system returns assets matching the selected metadata criteria
# {color:#FF991F}*[ NICE TO HAVE ]*{color} *GIVEN* an author filters assets by usage status
*WHEN* the Used filter is applied
*THEN* the system shall return assets referenced by at least one resource
*AND WHEN* the Unused filter is applied
*THEN* the system shall return assets not referenced by any resource.
# {color:#FF991F}*[ NICE TO HAVE ]*{color} *GIVEN* an author is inserting an asset into another resource in TAO 3.x
*WHEN* the user searches for assets used in a specific resource
*THEN* the system allows the user to identify assets referenced in a given item, or other supported resource
# {color:#FF5630}*[ MUST ]*{color} *GIVEN* an author is changing an asset already assigned to a resource in TAO 3.x
*WHEN* the user opens the asset search/selection dialog to replace the current asset
*THEN* the dialog opens in the folder containing the current asset, with that asset already selected
# {color:#FF5630}*[ MUST ]*{color} *GIVEN* an author is browsing the list of available assets
*WHEN* the user opens the asset search/selection dialog to add a new asset or replace the current asset
*THEN*  the assets shall be ordered alphabetically by asset name, using case-insensitive ascending sorting.
# {color:#FF5630}*[ MUST ]*{color} *GIVEN* the asset selection dialog displays a list of assets, with or without a search applied
*WHEN* the author selects a visible field as the sorting criterion
*THEN* the assets shall be ordered by the selected field
*AND* sorting shall be available for the following fields:
#* Label (case-insensitive alphabetic sorting, ascending and descending)
#* Location (case-insensitive alphabetic sorting, ascending and descending)
#* Last modified on (chronological order, ascending and descending)
{panel}

{panel:bgColor=#fffae6}

summary: Easier debugging of scoring rules
description:
*High level estimate (PdM): L*

To improve scoring troubleshooting, the proposal is to introduce an easier way to debug scoring at the test level for both manual and automatic scoring.

Today, troubleshooting scoring can be difficult. For complex scoring scenarios, easier test-level debugging would help users understand how final scores are produced, identify issues faster, and reduce reliance on technical rule inspection.

The scope should focus on:

* definition of a simpler test-level scoring debugging approach
* support for both manual and automatic scoring
* clearer visibility into how test-level scores are calculated
* validation that the proposed approach addresses the main scoring troubleshooting needs identified so far

{panel:bgColor=#eae6ff}
Some potential ideas that can help shape the solution:

* [https://oat-sa.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OAT/pages/4210458733/Visibility+of+Deliveries+for+external+users#FR3---Allow-direct-delivery-and-grading-preview-in-Authoring|https://oat-sa.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OAT/pages/4210458733/Visibility+of+Deliveries+for+external+users#FR3---Allow-direct-delivery-and-grading-preview-in-Authoring|smart-link] (FR3 - to allow direct grading preview in Authoring)
* [https://oat-sa.atlassian.net/browse/PCR-319|https://oat-sa.atlassian.net/browse/PCR-319|smart-link]  - as a mean to have multiple tabs available during the test preview (for Advance, Grader, etc.)
{panel}

summary: Improved alignment of bulleted or numbered lists
description:
{panel:bgColor=#deebff}
Currently, TAO provides options for text editing and list display, but the available formatting does not clearly support aligning the list marker itself together with the text in prompts. This creates inconsistent visual formatting when authors try to align bullet lists within interaction prompts. In particular, both center alignment and right alignment do not correctly align the bullet point or number together with the related text.

*Current behavior*

When authors apply center or right alignment to bulleted or numbered lists in areas using CKEditor, the text may appear aligned but the bullet point or number remains misaligned or left-positioned, resulting in inconsistent formatting.

*Desired behavior*

When authors apply left, center, or right alignment to a bulleted or numbered list in areas using CKEditor, both the list marker (bullet or number) and the related text should be aligned together as one visual unit.

!image-20260601-064557.png|width=615,alt="image-20260601-064557.png"!



*Why it matters*

Improves visual consistency; reduces manual formatting workarounds.

*Requirement*

TAO should support correct alignment of bulleted and numbered lists inside interaction prompts and, more generally, in any area where CKEditor is available, so that both the list marker and the related text are aligned together.

This feature extends the current formatting capabilities so that authors can align one or more words together with the bullet point or number, rather than aligning only the text content while leaving the marker misaligned. The improvement should provide a way to manage this formatting directly in CKEditor, improving layout consistency and reducing the need for manual formatting alternatives.
{panel}

{panel:bgColor=#eae6ff}
*As a* TAO author,

*I want to* be able to align bulleted or numbered text in any interaction and any place where CKEditor is available, including the bullet point or number itself
*so that* I can format consistently, improve presentation quality, and avoid manual workarounds.

*Scope*
-Common Interactions
-Text Block
-Graphic Interactions
-Text Reader PCI
-Text Block used in a passage
-Anywhere CKEditor is available
{panel}

{panel:bgColor=#e3fcef}
*Acceptance criteria* 

GIVEN an author creates a bulleted or numbered list in a CKEditor-enabled area,
WHEN the author applies left, center, or right alignment,
THEN the bullet/number and the related text are aligned together as one visual unit

GIVEN an author uses any area where CKEditor is available,
WHEN the content with an aligned bulleted or numbered list is saved, reopened, previewed, and delivered at runtime,
THEN the formatting is preserved and rendered consistently in authoring and at runtime
{panel}

summary: Line spacing formatting capability
description:
{panel:bgColor=#deebff}
{color:#FF5630}*[ TO BE VALIDATED ]*{color} 
Currently, TAO does not provide a native authoring option to configure interline spacing directly in the CKEditor. As a result, authors cannot control line spacing at authoring time and may need to rely on runtime-only accessibility tools or manual formatting workarounds.

*Why it matters*
Gives authors more control over readability and text layout; avoids reliance on runtime-only accessibility tools.



*Requirement*
TAO should allow authors to configure interline spacing directly in *Text Block*, *Text Reader*, and anywhere CKEditor is used during item authoring.

This feature extends the current text editing capabilities so that authors can define interline spacing according to their design needs directly inside the item editor. The improvement should provide a native authoring configuration for spacing between lines, rather than limiting this functionality to accessibility tools available only at delivery time. This would allow authors to better control readability, page layout, and text presentation from the start.
{panel}

{panel:bgColor=#eae6ff}
*As a* TAO author,

*I want to* to be able to configure interline spacing directly in *Text Block*, T*ext Reader*, and anywhere CKEditor is used,

*so that* I can control readability and text layout at authoring time according to the needs of the item.

*Scope*

-Text Reader PCI

-Text block

-Text block in a passage

-Common interactions (Match Interaction should be covered in [https://oat-sa.atlassian.net/browse/INV-1209|https://oat-sa.atlassian.net/browse/INV-1209|smart-link] [https://oat-sa.atlassian.net/browse/TETSN-263|https://oat-sa.atlassian.net/browse/TETSN-263|smart-link] )
-Graphic interactions

-Anywhere CKEditor is available
{panel}

{panel:bgColor=#e3fcef}
*Acceptance criteria* 

GIVEN an author is working in an area where CKEditor is available,

WHEN the author accesses the editor toolbar,

THEN the interline spacing commands are consistently available



GIVEN an author is working in an area where CKEditor is available,
WHEN the author selects an interline spacing option,
THEN the spacing between lines is applied to the selected text or paragraph in the editor



GIVEN an author uses any area where CKEditor is available,

WHEN the content with an interline spacing is saved, reopened, previewed, and delivered at runtime,

THEN the configured interline spacing is preserved and rendered consistently in authoring and at runtime in *TAO Advance*
{panel}

{panel:bgColor=#fffae6}
*Technical considerations*
This request may have different implementation implications depending on the editor version in use.
*CKEditor 4* does not appear to support interline spacing natively in the same way as more recent editor versions, so implementation may require a dedicated plugin/custom configuration.
*CKEditor 5* appears to offer more modern formatting extensibility and may support this capability more natively.

*_Analysis/estimation should therefore include_*:

# Validate CKEditor4 capabilities and if it is possible to add interline command to it
# Estimation of this approach
# Validate CKEditor5 capabilities and if it is possible migrate CKeditor4 to CKEditor5 without impact on Current Gen runtime
# Estimation of this approach
{panel}

summary: Extend text alignment capabilities across all interactions
description:
{panel:bgColor=#deebff}
At the moment, these editing and layout options are either unavailable or inconsistent depending on the interaction type. Some formatting controls are only available in specific components

*Why it matters*
Improves formatting consistency across item types; gives authors more flexibility in text presentation.

*Requirement*
TAO should extend text alignment to additional interactions wherever text formatting is supported.

This feature extends the current text alignment capabilities so that authors can apply text alignment consistently across different interaction types. The improvement should make justified alignment available anywhere CKEditor is used. This would reduce formatting limitations, improve consistency across items, and allow authors to better match the intended design of assessment content.
{panel}

{panel:bgColor=#eae6ff}
*As a* TAO author,

*I want* to be able to apply text alignment anywhere CKEditor is used

*so that* I can format text consistently across item types and improve the visual presentation of my items.

At the moment, these editing and layout options are either unavailable or inconsistent depending on the interaction type. Some formatting controls are only available in specific components, while others require workarounds or cannot be configured directly by the author.

*Scope*
-Common interactions
-Text block
-Graphic interactions
-Text Reader PCI
-Text block in a passage

-Anywhere CKEditor is available
{panel}

{panel:bgColor=#e3fcef}
*Acceptance criteria* 

GIVEN an author is working in an area where CKEditor is available,
WHEN the author accesses the editor toolbar,
THEN the text alignment commands are consistently available

GIVEN an author is working in an area where text alignment is supported,
WHEN the author applies right, left or justified alignment,
THEN the selected text or paragraph is aligned correctly in the editor

GIVEN an author uses any area where CKEditor is available,

WHEN the content with alignment configuration is saved, reopened, previewed, and delivered at runtime,

THEN the configured alignment is preserved and rendered consistently in authoring and at runtime in *TAO Advance*
{panel}

{panel:bgColor=#deebff}
*Note 1*
This request should therefore be considered mainly as a functional consistency check to ensure that, in the latest version, text alignment capabilities are correctly supported and rendered across all relevant areas in scope.
{panel}

summary: Text indentation formatting capability
description:
{panel:bgColor=#deebff}
{color:#FF5630}*[ TO BE VALIDATED ]*{color} 

Improvement of text editing capabilities to allow authors to apply and manage *indentation* directly in authoring.

At the moment, TAO does not provide a clear, consistent way for authors to manage indentation directly in the editor across all relevant areas in scope. This limits formatting control and may require manual layout workarounds.

*Why it matters*
Improves formatting control; supports clearer text hierarchy and better readability in text-based content.

*Requirement*
TAO should allow authors to apply indentation directly in the authoring editor, so that text can be structured more clearly and presented with better visual organization.

This feature extends the current text editing capabilities so that authors can control indentation natively during authoring. The improvement should support common indentation use cases such as managing the indentation of *paragraphs*, *bulleted and numbered lists*, structuring content more clearly, and improving the visual presentation of text. 

This would fill a gap in text formatting options and reduce the need for manual layout workarounds.
{panel}

{panel:bgColor=#eae6ff}
*As a* TAO author,

*I want* to be able to apply indentation directly in authoring

*so that* I can structure paragraphs and bulleted/numbered lists more clearly, improve readability, and avoid manual formatting workarounds.

*Scope:*

-Text Reader PCI

-Text block
-Text block in a passage
-Common interaction

-Graphic interaction

-Anywhere CKEditor is available
{panel}

{panel:bgColor=#e3fcef}
*Acceptance criteria* 

GIVEN an author is working in an area where CKEditor is available,
WHEN the author accesses the editor toolbar,
THEN the indentation commands are consistently available

GIVEN an author is working in an area where indentation is supported,
WHEN the author applies indentation,
THEN the content is indented correctly in the editor

GIVEN an author uses any area where CKEditor is available,

WHEN the content with indentation is saved, reopened, previewed, and delivered at runtime,
THEN the configured indentation is preserved and rendered in authoring and at runtime in *TAO Advance*
{panel}

{panel:bgColor=#fffae6}
*Technical considerations*

A quick check suggests that indentation may be available in both CKEditor 4 and CKEditor 5, but this should be formally validated during analysis.
{panel}

summary: Improve column width management and repeatability across items
description:
{panel:bgColor=#deebff}
Improvement of layout capabilities to allow authors to manage *Text Block and other interactions with more precision and consistency* across items.

At the moment, the width resizing does not provide a clear, measurable reference, so it is difficult for authors to reproduce the same width from one item to another with confidence. This leads to manual adjustments, inconsistent formatting across items, and unnecessary duplication when authors want to preserve the same layout.

*Why it matters*
Improves layout consistency; reduces repetitive manual work; makes it easier for authors to maintain a uniform presentation across items.
*Requirement*
TAO should allow authors to manage width resizing in a more measurable and repeatable way, so that the same width can be applied consistently across items without duplicating the item.

The improvement should support a reusable width reference, standard widths, or another UX solution that allows authors to reproduce the same width across multiple items in a consistent and reliable way. This would reduce layout inconsistencies, improve efficiency during authoring.

*UX Consideration* {color:#FF991F}*[ UX NEEDED ]*{color}
*_A UX proposal is needed_* to define the most appropriate way to give authors a clear and reusable width reference across items, for example through a ruler-like aid or another usable solution.
{panel}

{panel:bgColor=#eae6ff}
*As a* TAO author,
*I want* to be able to manage width resizing width more precisely and reuse the same width across items

*so that* I can maintain a consistent layout, reduce manual formatting work, and avoid duplicating items just to preserve the same sizing.
{panel}

{panel:bgColor=#e3fcef}
*Acceptance criteria*
GIVEN an author is working with an item,
WHEN the author resize the width,
THEN the width can be set in a more measurable and repeatable way than with the current visual resizing only

GIVEN an author wants to reproduce the same  width across multiple items,
WHEN the author applies the chosen width configuration,
THEN the same width can be applied consistently without duplicating an existing item
{panel}

summary: Granular column width management
Image resizing in Graphic Interactions
description:
{panel:bgColor=#deebff}
Improvement of authoring capabilities in *Graphic Interactions* to allow authors to resize the *background image* directly in the interaction editor, in line with the sizing flexibility available for media in other interaction types.

At the moment, the TAO permits selecting a background graphic for Graphic Interactions and placing hotspots, points, or related graphical areas on top of it, but does not allow resizing the background image directly in authoring.

*Why it matters*
Improves flexibility during authoring, supports better control of content layout, and increases consistency across interaction types.
{panel}

{panel:bgColor=#eae6ff}
*As a T*AO author*,*

*I want* to be able to resize background images in Graphic Interactions(Hotspot, Graphic Order, Graphic Associate, Graphic Gap, and Select Point) and have related hotspots, points, and graphical areas updated accordingly

*so that* I can better control the layout, adapt images to the intended presentation, and preserve the correct positioning of interactive areas without manual rework.
{panel}

{panel:bgColor=#e3fcef}
*Acceptance criteria* 

GIVEN an author is working in a Graphic Interaction that uses a background image,
WHEN the author resizes the background image in authoring,
THEN the image size is updated directly in the editor

GIVEN an author resizes the background image in a Graphic Interaction,
WHEN the related hotspots, points, or other graphical response areas already exist,
THEN those elements are repositioned and scaled accordingly so that they remain correctly aligned with the image

GIVEN an author uses a Graphic Interaction with a resized background image,
WHEN the content is saved, reopened, previewed, and delivered at runtime,
THEN the configured image size and the related graphical areas are preserved and rendered consistently in authoring and at runtime in both *Current Gen and TAO Advance.*
{panel}

summary: Size and position coordinates editing for hotspots and drop zones in Graphic Interactions

Better accessibility support for mathematical expressions
description:
{panel:bgColor=#deebff}
 {color:#FF5630}*[ TO BE VALIDATED ]*{color}
Improvement of math authoring capabilities to allow authors to insert fractions and other math expressions with a visual rendering comparable to *LaTeX / MathML*, while preserving correct *text-to-speech* output.

Currently, TAO provides math expressions through the *Formula Editor*. Authors currently lack an easy way to produce mathematical expressions that are both visually clear and correctly interpretable by assistive technologies.

Given the complexity of the request, further technical analysis is needed, as this requirement appears to go beyond a simple text editing enhancement and may require a more structured solution at rendering and accessibility level.

*Why it matters*
Improves both visual quality and accessibility for mathematical content, allowing authors to create expressions that are clear for readers and correctly interpretable by assistive technologies.
*Requirement*
TAO should provide a way for authors to insert fractions and other math expressions in regular content with high-quality visual rendering and reliable text-to-speech output.

This feature would extend the current math authoring capabilities by allowing authors to create mathematical content that is both visually robust and accessible, without relying on solutions that compromise text-to-speech compatibility.
{panel}

{panel:bgColor=#eae6ff}
*As a* TAO author*,*

*I want* to be able to insert fractions and other math expressions with high-quality visual rendering and correct text-to-speech output

*so that* I can create mathematical content that is both visually clear and accessible.
{panel}

{panel:bgColor=#e3fcef}
*Acceptance criteria* 

GIVEN an author is working in an area where mathematical content can be authored,
WHEN the author inserts a supported fraction or other supported math expression,
THEN the expression is rendered clearly and in a visually acceptable way in the editor

GIVEN an author uses supported mathematical content in authored text,
WHEN the content is saved, reopened, previewed, and delivered at runtime,
THEN the mathematical rendering is preserved and displayed consistently in authoring and at runtime in  *TAO Advance*

GIVEN an author uses supported mathematical content in authored text,
WHEN the content is read through text-to-speech or other assistive technology,
THEN the expression is interpreted correctly in an accessible way
{panel}

{panel:bgColor=#fffae6}
*Possible solution direction*
TAO should support a mechanism that allows mathematical expressions to be displayed with high visual quality while also permitting authors a way to provide a dedicated text alternative that can be used for text-to-speech purposes.

The text alternative should be stored with the mathematical expression in a way that ensures the expression remains both visually clear and accessible.

*Technical considerations*

This request *_requires significant technical validation_* before estimation.

The analysis should identify the most appropriate solution to support this behavior in authoring and runtime.

*UX consideration*

UX validation may be useful to determine how authors should create and edit accessible mathematical content in a usable way.

*Reference*: [https://oat-sa.atlassian.net/browse/TR-5878|https://oat-sa.atlassian.net/browse/TR-5878|smart-link] 
[https://oat-sa.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OAT/pages/2583199775|https://oat-sa.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OAT/pages/2583199775|smart-link] 
[https://help.learnosity.com/hc/en-us/articles/360017697818-Creating-accessible-math-content|https://help.learnosity.com/hc/en-us/articles/360017697818-Creating-accessible-math-content|smart-link] 
{panel}

description:
{panel:bgColor=#deebff}
{color:#36B37E}*[ PRODUCT FEATURE ]*{color} {color:#FF5630}*[ TAO3.X ]*{color}


Improvement of test authoring behavior so that newly inserted items in a *section* or *part* can automatically inherit the relevant flags/settings configured at *section* or *part* level.

Currently, newly added items do not automatically inherit the flags/settings from the parent section or part. From product perspective, this is the expected behavior, but for *INVALSI* it appears that up to *November 2023* items were inheriting those configurations automatically. This creates a discrepancy between past behavior and current behavior, and may lead to additional manual work and configuration inconsistencies.

*Why it matters*
Reduces repetitive manual configuration; improves consistency across items; aligns authoring behavior with previous INVALSI expectations.

*Requirement*
TAO should provide a way to apply section/part-level flags and settings to newly inserted items, or make this behavior configurable where needed.

This feature would improve authoring efficiency by reducing the need to manually reapply the same flags/settings to each newly created item. It should also ensure a more consistent configuration of items within the same section or part, especially in contexts where inheritance was previously expected.
{panel}

{panel:bgColor=#eae6ff}
*As a TAO author,*

*I want* newly inserted items in a section to inherit the relevant flags/settings from that section or part

*so that* I can avoid repetitive manual configuration and keep item settings consistent.
{panel}

{panel:bgColor=#e3fcef}
*Acceptance criteria*

# Newly added items automatically inherit item-level settings that are enabled on *all* existing items in the parent section
# Newly added items automatically inherit item-level settings that are enabled on *all* existing items in the parent test-part
# The following settings are supported by the inheritance mechanism:
#* Categories
#* Test-Taker Tools
#* Test navigation / Informational item usage
# A notification is displayed after adding a new item if one or more settings were inherited automatically mentioning the items and the settings inherited. {color:#00B8D9}*[ UX-NEEDED ]*{color} 
# Inherited settings are persisted after saving and reopening the test.
# Inherited settings are correctly reflected during test preview and runtime delivery.
{panel}

{panel:bgColor=#fffae6}
# *UX consideration (PdM and UX should define how the feature should be implemented before estimation)*
UX to define together with PdM how the feature should be implemented, (i.e.: adding an inherit flag)
# *Technical note*
From product perspective, the current non-inheritance behavior is understood to be expected.
However, for *INVALSI*, previous behavior reportedly allowed inheritance up to *November 2023*.
Analysis is therefore needed to clarify:
## whether this was a dedicated INVALSI customization,
## whether the behavior should be restored,
## or whether inheritance should be made explicitly configurable.
# The categories and the test-taker tools are set / persisted at the item level, but they are displayed visually in an aggregated way also to the section level, which explains the expectation they are inherited. However, there is no information set at the section level about the default or set categories and test-taker tools
{panel}

summary: Text alignment in Text Entry
Rotation of hotspots and drop zones in Graphic Interactions
description:
{panel:bgColor=#deebff}
{color:#36B37E}*[ PRODUCT FEATURE ]*{color} {color:#FF5630}*[ TAO3.X ]*{color}   {color:#FF5630}*[ TAO ADVANCE(NEXTGEN) ]*{color}

Improvement of graphic interaction authoring capabilities to allow authors to *rotate hotspots and drop zones*, instead of being limited to the default non-rotated shapes.

Currently, hotspots and drop zones can be positioned and resized, but not rotated. This limits the author’s ability to adapt the interactive area to the intended visual design. For example, a square cannot be used as a diamond shape at an arbitrary angle, even when that would better match the underlying graphic.

*Why it matters*
Improves flexibility in graphic authoring; allows better matching between interactive areas and the visual content; reduces the need for imprecise workarounds.

*Requirement*
TAO should allow authors to rotate hotspots and drop zones in Graphic Interactions.

This feature would extend the current graphic authoring capabilities by allowing authors to define the rotation angle of graphical response areas. The improvement should support use cases where a standard square or rectangular area needs to be displayed and used at a different angle, or where a rotated hotspot/drop zone would better fit the image structure.
{panel}

{panel:bgColor=#eae6ff}
*As a TAO author,*

*I want* to be able to rotate hotspots and drop zones in Graphic Interactions

*so that* I can better adapt the interactive areas to the visual layout and avoid workarounds when non-rotated shapes are not sufficient.
{panel}

{panel:bgColor=#e3fcef}
*Acceptance Criteria*

GIVEN an author is working in a Graphic Interaction with hotspots or drop zones,
WHEN the author applies a rotation to one of these elements,
THEN the selected hotspot or drop zone is rotated accordingly in the editor.

GIVEN an author uses a Graphic Interaction with rotated hotspots or drop zones,
WHEN the content is saved, reopened, previewed, and delivered at runtime,
THEN the configured rotation is preserved and rendered consistently in authoring and at runtime in *TAO Advance*.
{panel}

{panel:bgColor=#fffae6}
*Technical considerations*

Technical validation is required before estimation.

The analysis should identify the most appropriate solution to support rotation of hotspots and drop zones in authoring and runtime.



*UX consideration  (this can be done after high-level estimation)*

UX validation may be useful to determine how rotation should be exposed to authors in a usable way.

 
{panel}

summary: Configurable max-length warning in Text Entry
description:
{panel:bgColor=#deebff}
{color:#36B37E}*[ PRODUCT FEATURE ]*{color} {color:#FF5630}*[ TAO3.X ]*{color}  {color:#FF5630}*[ TAO ADVANCE(NEXTGEN) ]*{color}

Improvement of *Text Entry* behavior so that authors can keep a *maximum character constraint* while deciding whether the related TAO warning/instruction message is shown to the candidate.



Currently, TAO Advance provides the ability to “Remove Instructions” at item level, TAO-generated instructions from the following interactions: [+Choice+|https://userguide.taotesting.com/user-documentation/latest/public/choice-interaction], [+Order+|https://userguide.taotesting.com/user-documentation/latest/public/order-interaction], [+Associate+|https://userguide.taotesting.com/user-documentation/latest/public/associate-interaction], [+Match+|https://userguide.taotesting.com/user-documentation/latest/public/match-interaction], [+Hottext+|https://userguide.taotesting.com/user-documentation/latest/public/hottext-interaction], [+File Upload+|https://userguide.taotesting.com/user-documentation/latest/public/file-upload-interaction], [+Graphic Hotspot+|https://userguide.taotesting.com/user-documentation/latest/public/hotspot-interaction], [+Graphic Order+|https://userguide.taotesting.com/user-documentation/latest/public/graphic-order-interaction], [+Graphic Associate+|https://userguide.taotesting.com/user-documentation/latest/public/graphic-associate-interaction], or [+Graphic Select Point+|https://userguide.taotesting.com/user-documentation/latest/public/select-point-interaction] interactions (*existing feature for the above should be extended to Current Gen Test Runner*).

As a result, authors cannot currently keep the maximum character constraint active in Text Entry while independently controlling whether the related warning/instruction message is displayed.

!image-20260702-081800.png|width=379,alt="image-20260702-081800.png"!



*Why it matters*
Improves control over candidate-facing messaging; reduces unnecessary on-screen guidance when not desired; gives authors more flexibility in how Text Entry constraints are presented.

*Requirement*
TAO should allow authors to configure whether the warning/instruction message related to the maximum character constraint in *Text Entry* is displayed, independently from the constraint itself.

This feature would extend the current Text Entry configuration by separating:

* the *enforcement of the maximum character limit*
* from the *display of the related message/instruction*

This would allow authors to keep the validation behavior while deciding whether the candidate should see the related message.

*Scope*

* Text Entry
* Evaluate if this should be extended to other not covered interactions
{panel}

{panel:bgColor=#eae6ff}
*As a TAO author,*

*I want* to be able to keep the maximum character constraint in Text Entry while choosing whether the related warning/instruction message is shown

*so that* I can control the candidate experience more precisely without losing the validation rule.
{panel}

{panel:bgColor=#e3fcef}
*Acceptance Criteria*

GIVEN an author configures a maximum character constraint in a *Text Entry* interaction,
WHEN the author chooses to Remove Instruction,
THEN the maximum character constraint remains active but the message is not shown to the candidate.

GIVEN a Text Entry interaction is configured with a maximum character constraint and Remove Instruction,
WHEN the item is saved, reopened, previewed, and delivered at runtime,
THEN both the constraint behavior and the message visibility setting are preserved consistently in authoring and runtime.
{panel}

{panel:bgColor=#fffae6}
*Technical / Functional notes*

 None.
{panel}
